record.paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
record.context_brief: BRAVO for critically loaded finite-buffer GI/G/1/K queues
record.original_question: Consider a finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queue with one server, renewal arrivals, independent and identically distributed service times, K-1 waiting places, and loss of customers who arrive when the system is full. In the critically loaded case λ = μ, where c_a^2 and c_s^2 denote the squared coefficients of variation of the inter-arrival and service times, does the queue exhibit the BRAVO effect (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs), and in particular, for light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, is the long-run departure-process variability parameter γ* equal to (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)?

evidence.quote: A missing piece in the puzzle is the GI/G/1/K queue: Is there a BRAVO effect? If so, what is the variability? Does 1/3 play a role?
Conjecture 1 For the GI/G/1/K queue with λ = μ and light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, γ ∗ = 1/3 (c2_a + c2_s) + O(1/K).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (one server in service plus K−1 waiting positions). Customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2. Service times are i.i.d., independent of the arrival process, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. A customer who arrives to find the system full (K customers present) is lost. Let D(t) denote the number of customers that depart (i.e., complete service) by time t, and define the asymptotic variability parameter of the departure process by

  γ* := lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / (λ_eff · t),

where λ_eff is the effective throughput (departure rate) in steady state.

Assume the queue is critically loaded, i.e. λ = μ, and assume the interarrival and service time distributions are light-tailed (e.g. have finite moment generating functions in a neighborhood of 0).

(a) Does this system exhibit the BRAVO effect: namely, is γ* strictly smaller than the variability parameter that would arise in the corresponding stable or unstable (non-critical) regimes, due to the balancing of arrival and service rates?

(b) More precisely, prove or disprove the conjecture that, as K → ∞,

  γ* = (1/3) (c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture for the general GI/G/1/K critically loaded queue appears to remain open. While BRAVO has been established with the factor 1/3 for M/M/1/K (Markovian case) and with a factor (1−2/π) for the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical queue, recent work (e.g. on busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and on phase transitions in critically loaded queues) does not establish the 1/3 (c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) asymptotics for the general finite-buffer GI/G/1/K case. No located source claims a proof of the full conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues
status_evidence.snippet: Paper treats only M/M/1/K-type Markovian models; no proof of the GI/G/1/K conjecture is given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on critically loaded finite-buffer queues addresses Markovian cases, leaving the general GI/G/1/K conjecture unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: Studies critical GI/G/1 (infinite buffer) and BRAVO via busy periods.
status_evidence.claim: BRAVO is studied for the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical queue with factor (1-2/π), distinct from the finite-K 1/3 conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The asymptotic variance of departures in critically loaded queues
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes asymptotic variance results for certain critically loaded queues.
status_evidence.claim: Results cover specific model classes but do not settle the GI/G/1/K finite-buffer conjecture in full generality.
